title: The first Chinese bike that actually competes with the big boys

takeaways.text: Frame and bar cost about £1,600 delivered with tax from Panda Podium; his high-end build weighs about 6.8 kg and would cost roughly £4,000–5,000 new, or about £3,500 for a more modest build.
Despite being an aero frame it climbs very well, with a very stiff bottom bracket; it holds speed better than an Aethos and was manageable in 50 mph gusts with carbon-spoked wheels.
It is his favourite bike for descending, stable and locked-in through corners; comfort is good enough for all-day rides, though not at the level of the new SuperSix.
Build quality impressed his shop (faced brake mounts, clean interior); the only issues were a stiff front thru-axle and some headset creaking, possibly from repeatedly removing the bar for travel.
The stack (538 mm on his size) is 6 mm lower than a Tarmac SL8, so he runs many spacers; he would like a higher front end and finds the supplied bar's ergonomics only average.

disclosure: Owner video; he bought the frame and bar through Panda Podium and no sponsorship is stated. His Ultegra and FarSports build differs from the candidate's complete build.
summary: A UK rider's six-month review of a Quick Pro ER:ONE frame and bar built with Ultegra, after riding trips in Calpe and Mallorca.
